requirements: The core contributions of the paper 'Learning Performance-Improving Code Edits' have been reproduced.

sub_tasks.requirements: The gem5 simulator, compiler toolchain, and hardware/software environment required for deterministic performance measurement have been set up.
The gem5 full-system simulator is installed and configured to deterministically measure C++ program execution time.
Code has been implemented to install/build the gem5 full-system simulator from source (or via a pinned release) suitable for running C++ program binaries.

verification.spec: Run `gem5.opt --version` (or equivalent build binary) from the installation path and assert exit code 0 and version string is emitted. Also invoke gem5 with a trivial 'hello world' C++ binary configured for Skylake and assert it completes successfully.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Verbatim Intel Skylake gem5 configuration from https://github.com/darchr/gem5-skylake-config is obtained and integrated so simulations use this microarchitectural model.

verification.spec: Verify that the gem5-skylake-config repository from https://github.com/darchr/gem5-skylake-config is cloned/vendored into the project, that the Verbatim Intel Skylake configuration file (e.g., verbatim.py or config with Skylake parameters) exists, and that the gem5 runner script references this config file via CLI arguments or config loading. Check for presence of config file and grep for 'skylake' or 'Verbatim' in runner invocation code.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, given a compiled C++ binary and a test input, invokes gem5 with the Skylake config and returns a deterministic execution-time measurement (e.g., simulated cycles or seconds) used as the latency for all reported metrics.

verification.spec: Compile a small deterministic C++ program (e.g., prints sum of 1..1000) with the project's compile function, then call the gem5 runner twice with the same input. Assert both invocations return the exact same latency value (determinism) and that the value is a positive number in the expected units (cycles or seconds).

sub_tasks.requirements: Running the same binary on the same input through the gem5 runner twice yields identical reported execution times (bit-identical determinism).

verification.spec: Compile a small deterministic C++ program (e.g., prints sum from 1 to 1000) with GCC -O3 -std=c++17, then execute it through the gem5 runner twice with identical input. Assert that the two reported cycle/instruction counts (or execution time in simulated seconds) are bit-identical (equal as integers or strings).

sub_tasks.requirements: The gem5 runner enforces a 2-minute (per-test) timeout as described in Section 2 / Footnote 2, and treats timed-out runs as failures rather than allowing them to skew latency measurements.

verification.spec: Invoke the gem5 runner on a C++ program with an intentional infinite loop and a small test input. Assert the runner returns within roughly 2 minutes (plus small overhead), marks the run as timed-out/failed, and does NOT return a finite latency that could contaminate downstream latency aggregation.

sub_tasks.requirements: The C++ compiler toolchain used for all benchmarking is set up to exactly match the paper's configuration.
GCC version 9.3.0 is available and used as the compiler for all C++ programs in benchmarking.

verification.spec: Run `gcc --version` (or `g++ --version`) in the environment and verify that the reported version string contains '9.3.0'. Additionally grep the compile scripts/Dockerfile for explicit invocation of gcc/g++ 9.3.0 or pin to that version.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code that compiles benchmark programs invokes GCC with the C++17 standard and the -O3 optimization flag so measured speedups are on top of the optimizing compiler.

verification.spec: Grep the compilation scripts / Makefile / Python code responsible for compiling C++ benchmark programs and verify the g++/gcc invocation includes both `-std=c++17` and `-O3` flags.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that takes a source C++ program, compiles it with the above toolchain/flags to a binary suitable for gem5 execution, and surfaces compilation failures distinctly from runtime failures.

verification.spec: Call the compilation wrapper on (a) a valid C++17 program and assert a binary path is returned with compile_status='ok'; (b) a syntactically broken C++ program and assert the wrapper returns a compile-failure status distinct from any runtime-failure status.

sub_tasks.requirements: A benchmarking harness ties compilation, gem5 execution, test-case checking, and latency logging together for slow/fast program pairs.

Code has been implemented that, for a given program, runs all associated test-case inputs through the gem5 runner, records per-test correctness (output match) and per-test latency, and aggregates latency across test cases for use as time(y).

verification.spec: Provide a compiled program and 3 mock test-case inputs/outputs. Call the per-program evaluation function. Assert the returned structure contains per-test correctness booleans, per-test latencies, and an aggregated latency (sum or mean) used as time(y). Verify aggregation is over the retained test cases.

sub_tasks.requirements: The harness supports parallel execution across multiple CPU cores/workers so the large number of required simulations can be completed in reasonable wall-clock time.

verification.spec: Invoke the batch gem5 evaluation harness on a small workload of N programs with num_workers=1 and num_workers>=4. Assert wall-clock time is meaningfully lower with more workers and that results are identical (deterministic). Confirm the harness exposes a parallelism/worker-count parameter.

sub_tasks.requirements: The infrastructure is capable of executing the scale of gem5 simulations reported in the paper (on the order of the 42.8 million simulations used to relabel PIE runtimes), demonstrated by successfully running the full dataset relabeling / evaluation pipeline end-to-end.

verification.spec: Run the end-to-end dataset relabeling / evaluation pipeline on the provided PIE dataset (or a documented replica subset) and confirm it completes without crash, producing per-program gem5 latencies for the reported ~77K train / 2.5K val / 978 test programs. Since fully running 42.8M simulations exceeds the budget, verify the harness reports a projected simulation count on this order and successfully processes a representative slice (e.g., the 978-example test set).

sub_tasks.requirements: Supporting hardware/software resources for training and self-play data generation are provisioned.

A multi-GPU training environment (e.g., 8x48GB GPUs such as NVIDIA RTX A6000 or L40) with HuggingFace Transformers and FSDP is set up to fine-tune the 7B and 13B CODELLAMA variants as described in Appendix A.8.

verification.spec: On the training machine, run `nvidia-smi` and assert >=1 GPU with sufficient memory is visible. Import torch/transformers and instantiate a FSDP-wrapped small CodeLlama-7B stub (or launch a 1-step training smoke test on a tiny batch) using the project's training script; assert the script completes step 1 without OOM.

sub_tasks.requirements: A multi-core CPU environment with sufficient RAM (comparable to a 24-core Intel 13900k with 64GB RAM per Appendix A.6) is available and used for the self-play synthetic-data execution/equivalence checking pipeline.

verification.spec: Invoke the self-play synthetic-data generation pipeline's execution/equivalence-checking module on a small batch of candidate synthetic (input,output) pairs using multiprocessing. Assert it completes successfully utilizing multiple worker processes (as configured in code) and returns correct equivalence labels.

sub_tasks.requirements: The hyperfine-based real-hardware benchmarking baseline used to motivate gem5 is set up so its variance claims can be reproduced.
The hyperfine Rust benchmarking tool is installed and callable from the evaluation infrastructure for the identical-program variance study.

verification.spec: Run `hyperfine --version` from the evaluation environment and assert exit code 0 and version string. Also run `hyperfine --runs 3 'true'` and assert it completes and reports mean/std timings.

sub_tasks.requirements: The PIE dataset of performance-improving C++ program pairs (train/val/test splits with test cases) has been constructed from CodeNet with gem5-based runtime annotations.
Raw CodeNet C++ submissions are ingested and filtered to keep only accepted programs organized as per-user, per-problem chronological trajectories.
Code has been implemented to load CodeNet C++ submissions and group them by (user_id, problem_id), producing per-user chronological sequences Y^u = [y_1^u, y_2^u, ...] sorted by submission timestamp.

verification.spec: Feed the dataset-loading function a small mock CodeNet directory with multiple (user_id, problem_id, timestamp, code) rows in shuffled order. Assert the returned data structure groups submissions by (user_id, problem_id) and each group's list is sorted ascending by timestamp, matching Y^u = [y_1^u, y_2^u, ...].

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to filter each trajectory to only accepted submissions (removing programs that failed unit tests or exceeded the time limit), yielding the accepted trajectory Y* = [y_1*, ..., y_n*].

verification.spec: Provide the trajectory-filtering function with a mock user trajectory containing accepted, WA (wrong-answer), and TLE submissions (per CodeNet status codes). Assert the returned Y* contains only accepted submissions in original chronological order and excludes all non-accepted ones.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to restrict data to C++ programs only, since C++ is the performance-oriented language compatible with the gem5 simulator used in this work.

verification.spec: Pass the dataset-construction language filter a mix of submissions labeled 'C++', 'Python', 'Java', 'C'. Assert the output contains only rows with language == C++ (and its recognized aliases such as 'C++14'/'C++17'), and none of the other languages.

sub_tasks.requirements: Slow-fast program pairs are constructed from each accepted trajectory using the >10% relative runtime improvement criterion.
Code has been implemented to enumerate all ordered pairs (y_i, y_j) with i<j from each accepted trajectory Y* as candidate (slow, fast) pairs.

verification.spec: Give the pair-enumeration function an accepted trajectory of length n=4. Assert the returned set of candidate pairs equals {(y_i, y_j) : 0 <= i < j < 4}, i.e., 6 ordered pairs, matching the paper's construction P=(y1,y2),(y1,y3),(y2,y3),...

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to keep only pairs where (time(y_i) - time(y_j)) / time(y_i) > 0.10 using gem5-measured runtimes, discarding all others.

verification.spec: Feed the pair-filtering function synthetic pairs with known gem5 runtimes: (100,89) => keep (11% improvement), (100,91) => drop (9%), (100,90) => drop (exactly 10%, strict >). Assert output pair set matches expected.

sub_tasks.requirements: Each C++ program is annotated with a gem5-measured execution time (replacing CodeNet's inconsistent CPUTime), and the annotation pipeline is scaled to the required number of simulations.
Code has been implemented to compile each C++ program with GCC 9.3.0, C++17, and -O3, and execute the resulting binary under gem5 to record per-program deterministic runtimes used as time(y) labels.

verification.spec: Invoke the compilation function on a simple valid C++17 program and inspect the actually-executed command line. Assert it uses `g++` (version 9.3.0), includes flags `-std=c++17` and `-O3`. Then run the produced binary under gem5 and assert a numeric time(y) is recorded.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to enforce a 2-minute timeout per gem5 simulation and mark programs exceeding this as timed-out so they are excluded from pair construction.

verification.spec: Run the gem5 wrapper on a program that intentionally exceeds 2 minutes of simulated execution; assert the wrapper terminates in ~2 minutes wall-clock, returns a 'timeout' status, and that the pair-construction stage excludes programs bearing timeout status from candidate (slow, fast) pairs.

sub_tasks.requirements: The dataset is split into train/validation/test by problem_id with no problem overlap, matching the paper's counts.

verification.spec: Run the splitting function on a mock set of problems and pairs. Assert (a) the intersection of problem-id sets across train/val/test splits is empty, and (b) every pair is assigned to the same split as its associated problem-id, with no pair straddling splits.

verification.spec: Load the constructed PIE train/val/test pair files and count the number of (slow, fast) pairs in each split. Assert train == 77967, val == 2544, test == 978 (within tolerance).

sub_tasks.requirements: The high-quality (HQ) subset and per-test-example fastest-human-submission reference used downstream are derived from the base PIE dataset.

verification.spec: Run the HQ-subset construction function on the full PIE training dataset. Assert: (a) for each problem, at most 4 pairs are retained, (b) the retained pairs per problem are those with the highest measured speedup, (c) the total number of pairs equals 4085, and (d) the average pairs-per-problem is 2.77. Report total pair count as the measured value.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to record, for every test-set problem, the fastest human-submission execution time (over all CodeNet accepted submissions for that problem) alongside the pair, for use as an upper-bound reference.

verification.spec: Load the test-set data file. Assert every test example row includes a field (e.g., 'fastest_human_time' or similar) that is a positive numeric latency, and that this value is <= the min gem5-measured runtime among the test example's associated slow/fast programs (since it aggregates over ALL CodeNet accepted submissions for the problem, it should not exceed any single submission's time).

sub_tasks.requirements: The final dataset artifacts are packaged with per-pair metadata linking each pair to its problem_id, test cases, and gem5-measured source/target runtimes.

Code has been implemented to serialize each split as records containing at least: src_code, tgt_code, problem_id, user_id, src_gem5_time, tgt_gem5_time, and measured speedup, enabling downstream training and evaluation.

verification.spec: Load each of train/val/test serialized dataset files and verify each record contains keys: src_code, tgt_code, problem_id, user_id, src_gem5_time, tgt_gem5_time, and speedup. Verify src_code/tgt_code are non-empty strings, times are positive floats, and speedup equals src_gem5_time/tgt_gem5_time (within 1e-3).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to associate each pair with the set of unit tests for its problem_id so that correctness checking during evaluation and dataset construction uses the exact tests linked to that problem.

verification.spec: For a sample of 10 dataset pairs, invoke the test-lookup function with each pair's problem_id and confirm it returns a non-empty list of (stdin, expected_stdout) unit test cases. Verify that the tests returned for different problem_ids are distinct and that the same problem_id always returns the same test set.

sub_tasks.requirements: Test cases including CodeNet base tests and AlphaCode-generated tests are collected, filtered by gem5 timeout constraints, and integrated to produce per-problem test suites used for correctness evaluation across train/validation/test splits.

Code has been implemented to load the CodeNet-provided unit tests (approximately 4 per problem on average) for each competitive programming problem in PIE.

verification.spec: Invoke the CodeNet test-case loader for at least 20 problem_ids appearing in PIE. Verify that at least 90% return non-empty test lists, and that the mean count across sampled problems is ≥3 (paper reports ~4 CodeNet tests/problem on average).

verification.spec: Invoke the AlphaCode test-case loader for at least 20 problem_ids appearing in PIE. Verify that AlphaCode-generated tests are loaded and are distinguishable (e.g., via source tag) from CodeNet tests, and that at least some problems get many additional tests (>10) beyond CodeNet's ~4.

verification.spec: Run the test-case filtering pipeline twice on the same raw inputs (same seed if applicable) and verify that the resulting per-problem test suites are byte-identical (or set-equal) across the two runs.

sub_tasks.requirements: The final filtered per-problem test suites match the reported median counts per split.
The median number of test cases per problem in the training set after filtering matches the reported value of 82.5.

verification.spec: For each problem in the training split, count the number of test cases attached to it (after filtering out cases that lead to gem5 timeouts >2 min). Compute the median across problems and assert it equals 82.5 within tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: The median number of test cases per problem in the validation set after filtering matches the reported value of 75.

verification.spec: For each problem in the validation split, count the number of test cases attached to it. Compute the median across problems and assert it equals 75 within tolerance.

Then verify that when all tests pass it returns 'correct'. Confirms 'reject the program if a single test fails'.

sub_tasks.requirements: Instruction, few-shot, and chain-of-thought prompting strategies are implemented as described in Section 3.1.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that for a given source (slow) C++ program from the PIE test set, the instruction prompt correctly substitutes the source code into the `{src_code}` slot and returns a single prompt string suitable for a single-turn LLM query (no few-shot examples appended).
